main_result: Theorem 1.1 (Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture): with k = 2^75, for every N, every p in (0,1) and every family D in 2^[N], if mu_p(D) >= 1 - 1/k then the exceptional family E_k(D) (sets not contained in any union of k members of D, repeats allowed) is p-small. Here p-small means there is a cover G of E_k(D) with sum over I in G of p^|I| at most 1/2. The paper also states a positive-selector corollary (via Markov) and a two-union corollary with density loss p/C, C = 50*512^4, which depends on cited results.
proof_strategy: The argument has three layers. (1) Proposition 3.1 (Section 3): for q with mu_q(F) >= 1/2, E_32(F) is (q/2^70)-small. It uses biased Fourier weights b(U), w(U)=b(U)^2, with a Parseval bound sum q^|U| w(U) <= 1, and a signed 32-row product identity giving sum over nonempty U subset of S of w(U)^16 >= 2^-32 for every exceptional S. (2) Lemma 2.1 (Section 2): a probabilistic covering lemma. Sets with huge weight are covered directly; the remaining weight bins are covered by sampled unions of pairs, plus residual tuple-unions, with expected cost controlled by a recursion on weighted tuple sums W_t. (3) Section 4: a coupling of L = 2^70 rows, each with law mu_p, whose union has law mu_q with q = Lp (Case 1), or whose union is the full ground set (Case 2). Union bound gives all rows in D with probability at least 31/32; then E_32(F) = E_{32L}(D) and Proposition 3.1 yields density q/L = p. I checked each displayed inequality in Sections 2–4 and found them correct as written; the weakest links are the citation-dependent steps in the corollaries.
hardest_part: The two-union corollary (Corollary 1.3 and its proof). It chains several external results (Li Corollary 3.1, Park Theorem 3.4, OpenAIThreshold26 Theorem 1.1) whose hypotheses are never stated, and the factor r = p/2 is not explained. I could not confirm that E_2(D) meets the hypotheses of those results from mu_p(D) > 1/2. In the self-contained parts, the most intricate bookkeeping was the recursion W_{t+1} <= T(1+rm)^r W_t in Lemma 2.1 and the signed identity in Proposition 3.1; I checked both and found no error, but they are the places where a slip would be easiest to miss.

main_result: For k=2^75 and any family D of subsets of [N] with Bernoulli-p measure at least 1-1/k, the family E_k(D) of sets not contained in any union of k members of D is p-small: it has a cover G with sum over G of p^{|I|} at most 1/2. The proof reduces to a fixed-density statement (Proposition 3.1: if mu_q(F) >= 1/2 then E_32(F) is (q/2^70)-small) and then recovers density p by a row-coupling. Two corollaries are also stated: a two-union version with constant density loss (Corollary 1.2), and a consequence for positive selectors, where {S: phi(S) >= k^2 M} is p-small. The core chain (Lemma 2.1, the signed 32-row identity, the bin/cover construction, and both cases of the coupling) I checked line by line and found consistent. The corollary and the related-work comparisons depend on external results I could not check.
proof_strategy: Parseval applied to the biased Fourier coefficients gives a global bound sum_U q^{|U|} w(U) <= 1 on the squared weights w(U)=b(U)^2. A signed 32-row array of column masses, built so that the all-zero column has zero mass, gives the identity sum_{U subset S} (-1)^{|U|} b(U)^{32} = 0 for each S in E_32(F), and hence sum_{nonempty U subset S} w(U)^16 >= 2^{-32}. Weights are split into a large-weight class G_0 (cost at most 2^-6) and dyadic bins H_{r,h}, each covered by Lemma 2.1 (random pair sampling with a residual-tuple step, cost at most 3*2^-h). A set that contains no generator has 16th-power weight sum below 2^-32, which contradicts the identity, so the union of covers covers E_32(F) at density q/2^70. Density is restored by a coupling: in Case 1 (Lp<1) each of L rows is a Bernoulli-p set and their union is Bernoulli-Lp, so E_32(F)=E_k(D); in Case 2 (Lp>=1) a mandatory-row coupling makes some L rows in D cover [N], forcing E_k(D) empty. The corollary's fractional-to-integral chain and the positive-selector deduction rely on cited external results whose hypotheses I could not check; that part is unclear to me.
hardest_part: The transfer in Corollary 1.2 from the hypothesis mu_p(D)>1/2 to Li's fractional cover at density r=p/2, and then to an integral cover through the companion threshold theorem. Each step depends on external statements (Li Cor. 3.1 / Thm 1.9, Park Thm 3.4 / Cor. 3.5, OpenAIThreshold26 Thm 1.1) whose hypotheses are not restated, so I cannot verify that the corollary's hypotheses match them. In the self-contained part, the most error-prone step was the 32-row signed expansion, which I reconstructed with the sign and per-row factorization checked by hand, but the write-up skips the intermediate lines.

main_result: Set k=2^75. If an arbitrary family D on [N] has product measure mu_p(D) >= 1-1/k, then E_k(D) (sets not contained in any union of k members of D, repeats allowed) has a cover G with sum over I in G of p^|I| <= 1/2. Section 1 adds a positive-selector consequence via Markov's inequality, and a Corollary (not fully self-contained) gives an E_2 cover at density p/C when mu_p(D) > 1/2, using cited results of Li, Park and an OpenAI threshold paper.
proof_strategy: The main proof has three layers. (1) Lemma 2.1 is a self-contained probabilistic covering lemma: it removes high-weighted-degree sets, samples random pair unions, and bounds residual tuples by a product of extension weights; I checked the exponent bookkeeping and it closes for h >= 64. (2) Proposition 3.1 expands the indicator of F in the biased Fourier basis, giving sum_U q^|U| w(U) <= 1 by Parseval, and uses a 32-row signed array with column mass P - (1-q)^32(-1)^{sum y} to show each exceptional set carries sum of w(U)^16 >= 2^-32; the dyadic bins of w then feed Lemma 2.1, and I verified the resulting cost bound 1/64 + 6/(2^64-1) < 1/2. (3) Section 4 couples L=2^70 product rows through a sparse union (case Lp<1) or a mandatory-row construction (case Lp>=1) so that the union of rows has law mu_q with q=Lp and E_32(F)=E_k(D). The Corollary and the Section 1 Markov argument depend on cited results whose hypotheses I could not match.
hardest_part: The Corollary's transfer from mu_p(D) > 1/2 to Li's fractional result at density r = p/2, together with the cited rounding theorem, which is not stated in enough detail for me to check. For the main theorem I re-derived the signed identity in Proposition 3.1 and the residual-tuple bound in Lemma 2.1 line by line and found no gap, but I relied on the exact Fourier normalization and the ordering of the pair-sampling independence, which I checked by hand rather than by computer.
